title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building a set-theoretic model (the 'analogie ensembliste') for a formalism he calls 'ateliers' (chapter IX). The previous page treats correspondences: a correspondence alpha between sets E and E' has a graph Gamma ⊂ E×E', with projections f: Gamma→E and f': Gamma→E'. So alpha factors as alpha = f' ∘ ^t f. The factor ^t f is a 'comorphism', acting by A ↦ f^{-1}(A). The factor f' is a 'morphism', acting by B ↦ f'(B). The induced map is alpha_*: P(E)→P(E'), alpha_*(A) = f'(f^{-1}(A)), the direct image of A under the relation. Such a map always commutes with arbitrary unions, and sup-preserving maps P(E)→P(E') correspond exactly to relations. The question is which extra preservation properties single out special correspondences.

Proposition A (equivalent conditions):
(i) alpha_* preserves disjointness (the symbol |∘|, as confirmed on the next page by 'S|∘|T ⟺ alpha(S)|∘|alpha(T)').
(ii) alpha_* commutes with S∧T, and with ⋂_{i∈I} S_i for I ≠ ∅.
(ii') and (iii') alpha_* commutes with relative complement S∧∁T.
(iii) alpha_* commutes with S∧∁T for T ≤ S.
(iv) f' is injective. Equivalently, alpha is a comorphism followed by the morphism of an injective map. Equivalently, alpha is the transpose of a partial map g: E' ⊇ f'(Gamma) → E, with alpha_*(A) = g^{-1}(A).

Proof sketch:
- (iv) ⇒ all others: preimage under a partial map preserves intersections, differences and disjointness.
- (i) ⇒ (iv): apply (i) to singletons. alpha_*({e1}) ∩ alpha_*({e2}) = ∅ for e1 ≠ e2, so each e' is related to at most one e.

Corollary 1: add the condition alpha_*(1) = 1, i.e. every e' is related to something.
- (i) disjointness plus 1↦1.
- (ii) binary meets plus 1↦1.
- (ii') finite intersections, including the empty one.
- On the next page: (ii) arbitrary intersections, (iii) complement, (iv) alpha_* = g^{-1} for a total map g: E'→E.
Thus the complete Boolean homomorphisms P(E)→P(E') are exactly the preimage maps of maps E'→E.

The page then goes on (next page) to B, the analogous characterisation of f' surjective, and further corollaries. Purpose: to identify, inside the 'atelier' formalism, intrinsic lattice-theoretic characterisations of morphisms, comorphisms and their injective/surjective variants, mirroring the factorisation question raised on the previous page.
errors: (ii) needs I ≠ ∅, which he correctly notes: the empty intersection would force alpha_*(1) = 1, which is the extra condition of the Corollary.

Lines (ii') and (iii') as transcribed are duplicates; one is presumably a variant (e.g. plain complement ∁T versus relative complement). No mathematical error, but the list is unfinished or redundant.

On the following page the conclusion of Corollary 1 is called 'alpha est un isomorphisme' with the gloss 'f: E ≃ E''. What is actually characterised is f': Gamma ≃ E' (alpha is the comorphism of a total map g: E'→E), not an isomorphism E ≃ E'. This looks like a slip of wording.

ideas.what: Correspondences (relations) E→E' as union-preserving maps P(E)→P(E'), factored as a comorphism ^t f followed by a morphism f' through the graph
ideas.modern_name: Rel ≃ free sup-lattices; span/graph factorisation of a relation

ideas.what: A relation's direct image preserves disjointness / binary meets / differences iff the relation is the inverse of a partial map
ideas.modern_name: characterisation of partial maps among relations (meet-preserving sup-maps between powersets)

ideas.what: Adding top-preservation: alpha_* preserves all meets / complement iff alpha_* = g^{-1} for a total map g: E'→E
ideas.modern_name: Set^op ≃ complete atomic Boolean algebras (Lindenbaum–Tarski duality)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains standard, correct characterisations of partial and total maps among relations via lattice-preservation properties of P(E)→P(E'). These are classical. The only historically interesting point is that they serve as a set-theoretic model for Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 'ateliers' formalism, but the mathematics on this page itself is routine.
